modules.heading: Typography and Letterform Analysis
modules.description: Study type roles, forms, scale, spacing, legibility, and interaction with surrounding visuals.
focus_questions: How do type roles and scale establish priority?
Which letterform, spacing, wrapping, or contrast traits affect readability?
How does type interact with imagery and other text?

modules.heading: Hero Visual Analysis
modules.description: Study a dominant person, object, photograph, or illustration and its role in the poster.
focus_questions: What visible subject or image anchors attention?
How do scale, crop, pose, contrast, and placement support its role?
How does the hero relate to the message and supporting information?

modules.heading: Colour Relationships
modules.description: Study a distinctive palette, contrast system, saturation, temperature, or color-coded function.
focus_questions: Which color relationships separate or connect components?
How do value and saturation affect readability and hierarchy?
Which contextual color interpretations remain uncertain?

modules.heading: Directional Guidance and Visual Flow
modules.description: Study lines, repeated shapes, gaze, diagonals, or implied movement that guide attention.
focus_questions: Which visible cues suggest a direction or sequence?
How does the eye path connect the message, subject, and information?
Where does flow become ambiguous or compete with reading order?

modules.heading: Layering and Depth
modules.description: Study overlap, foreground/background separation, masking, and depth cues.
focus_questions: Which components overlap or sit in distinct visual planes?
What makes the layering appear intentional?
Does depth improve focus or obscure important content?

modules.heading: Negative Space Utilization
modules.description: Study open areas, isolation, margins, and the role of unoccupied space.
focus_questions: Where are the largest open regions?
How do they isolate, group, or balance components?
Does open space support the communication task?

modules.heading: Illustration and Visual Metaphors
modules.description: Study illustration style, symbolism, and image-based metaphor without treating interpretation as fact.
focus_questions: What is directly depicted, and which readings are interpretations?
How does the illustration relate to the message or mood?
Which visual metaphor hypotheses have supporting evidence?

modules.heading: Branding and Identity
modules.description: Study visible logos, identity systems, and repeated brand cues.
focus_questions: Which marks or repeated cues visibly identify a brand?
How are brand elements integrated with the message?
What identity claims cannot be confirmed from the poster alone?

modules.heading: Information Density
modules.description: Study how multiple information blocks are grouped, prioritized, and made readable.
focus_questions: How many distinct information groups compete for attention?
How are related details grouped and prioritized?
Which details are difficult to scan or read?

modules.heading: Grid and Alignment
modules.description: Study repeated edges, columns, baselines, and modular information structures.
focus_questions: Which edges, baselines, or columns appear aligned?
How does the underlying structure group content?
Where do deviations create emphasis or inconsistency?

modules.heading: Texture and Surface Treatment
modules.description: Study prominent material texture, grain, halftone, print effects, or surface overlays.
focus_questions: Which surface qualities are directly visible?
How does texture affect contrast, depth, or mood?
Does texture interfere with text or component clarity?

modules.heading: Component Interaction and Attention Competition
modules.description: Study multiple high-salience components that may reinforce or compete with one another.
focus_questions: Which components compete for attention, and by what visible means?
Do their messages reinforce or interrupt one another?
Which relationship has the greatest effect on reading order?
